blocks.x: Blockchain & Digital Trust inside Logistics & Supply Chain: what the sector's controls demand, what we build on the platform rails, and the outcomes written into the engagement.

In Logistics & Supply Chain, blockchain & digital trust delivers distributed-ledger programs where a shared, verifiable record has economic value: enterprise dlt networks for multi-party workflows, asset tokenization, smart contract engineering and audit, provenance and traceability, decentralized identity with verifiable credentials, and on-chain analytics for compliance. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: enterprise dlt network engineering, asset tokenization & digital assets, smart contract engineering & audit — delivered on Dataq Ledger and Dataq Sentinel with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: EUDR-grade due diligence and custody evidence for high-value goods remain paper-based; customs and buyers escalate.
Carrier portals, EDI and telematics produce a patchwork; the control tower reads yesterday. Exceptions surface as customer complaints.
Planners re-plan routes and loads by hand when trucks break down or orders change; exception queues eat capacity that should improve the network.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

Under the hood the pattern composes 6 Blockchain & Digital Trust services — Enterprise DLT Network Engineering, Asset Tokenization & Digital Assets, Smart Contract Engineering & Audit, Provenance, Traceability & Supply Chain Trust as the usual core — sequenced by the Dataq Method, with CMR/ADR/IMDG transport rules obligations shaping design decisions from the first sprint onward.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Permissioned networks for multi-party truth: governance, consensus and integration done institutionally.
Instruments as tokens: issuance, custody and lifecycle under securities-law discipline.
Contracts as production software: specification, formal verification and audit before value moves.
Proof, not paperwork: EUDR, DPP and chain-of-custody systems regulators and customers can verify.
Anchored custody events for in-scope commodities with regulator interfaces (due-diligence evidence in hours)
Shared evidence between shipper, carrier and insurer (claims and disputes collapse)
Hours instead of days via agentic remediation

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: CMR/ADR/IMDG transport rules and EUDR. Deforestation due diligence for in-scope commodities with evidence duties. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

This capability runs on the cadence set out below; the rhythm is fixed, the scope is signed. Weeks 1–2 belong to measurement: the baseline metric is captured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 run a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — steered by a control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 convert the pilot into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, and close with a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses a gate is stopped or redirected on the record.
